gate.wording_precommitted: Does the novelty pass establish that the literature does NOT already answer the placement question (which structural feature of the hierarchy flips blow-up on, and where 3D NS sits relative to that flip)?
gate.branch_fired: no -> Report the literature's answer, links not counts, and STOP. This closes route 5 at the placement-question level; no construction warranted.
gate.realization_named_per_lesson_91: The Katz-Pavlovic / Friedlander-Pavlovic dyadic system in the reduced form given by Cheskidov arXiv:math/0601074 eq. (1.1): d/dt u_n + nu*lambda^(2*alpha*n)*u_n - lambda^n*u_{n-1}^2 + lambda^(n+1)*u_n*u_{n+1} = g_n, u_0 = 0, lambda > 1, with alpha the dissipation degree; together with the sabra shell model in Constantin-Levant-Titi's realization and the Fourier-restricted models in Miller's. This is a statement about the published literature on those named models, NOT about 3D Navier-Stokes.

placement_of_3D_NS.headline: 3D Navier-Stokes sits at dissipation degree alpha = 2/5 in the Katz-Pavlovic dyadic hierarchy, strictly inside the hierarchy's own undecided window (1/3, 1/2).
placement_of_3D_NS.source_read_from: e-print LaTeX source (dyadic1.tex, dated 2006-06-08), NOT the abstract — the abstract does not contain the alpha = 2/5 calibration at all
placement_of_3D_NS.calibration_quote_verbatim: Note that for $\alpha=2/5$ the following are sharp estimates on the inertial term: $|(B(u,u),Au)| \lesssim |Au|^{3/2}|A^{1/2}u|^{3/2}$, where $(\cdot,\cdot)$ and $|\cdot|$ are the $l^2$-inner product and norm respectively. The best known estimates on the inertial term of the 3D NSE are the same, with $(\cdot,\cdot)$ and $|\cdot|$ being the $L^2$-inner product and norm.
placement_of_3D_NS.dimension_axis_quote_verbatim: It is remarkable that in the critical case $\alpha =1/3$ the following are sharp estimates on the nonlinear term: $|(B(u,u),Au)| \lesssim |Au|^{2}|A^{1/2}u|$. Note that the best known estimates on the nonlinear term of the 4D NSE are exactly the same.
placement_of_3D_NS.openness_quote_verbatim: Note that there is still a gap between the regions of global regularity and blow-up in finite time, which means that the developed technique is not sharp enough to separate these two behaviors.
placement_of_3D_NS.same_open_question_quote_verbatim: In this paper we study a dyadic model, which has similar properties to the 3D NSE, the same estimates on the inertial term, and the same open question concerning the regularity of the solutions.

evidence.title: Analytic Study of Shell Models of Turbulence
evidence.finding: GLOBAL REGULARITY for the viscous sabra shell model, plus a finite dimensional global attractor and globally invariant inertial manifolds
evidence.quote_verbatim: We prove the global regularity of solutions and show that the shell model has finitely many asymptotic degrees of freedom, specifically: a finite dimensional global attractor and globally invariant inertial manifolds.

evidence.title: A Note on the Regularity of Inviscid Shell Model of Turbulence
evidence.finding: inviscid sabra: global weak solutions, short-time uniqueness, BKM-type blow-up criterion, Onsager analogue under |u_n| <= C k_n^(-1/3) (sqrt(n) log(n+1))^(-1), and GLOBAL REGULARITY in the 'two-dimensional' parameter regime

evidence.title: Regularizing Effect of the Forward Energy Cascade in the Inviscid Dyadic Model
evidence.finding: forward energy cascade REGULARIZES: every solution must have 3/5 L^2-based (or 1/10 L^3-based) regularity for all positive time; conjectured up to Onsager's 5/6 (L^2-based) and 1/3 (L^3-based)

evidence.title: An inviscid dyadic model of turbulence: the fixed point and Onsager's conjecture
evidence.finding: unique equilibrium; EVERY forced solution blows up in finite time in H^{5/6}; Onsager's conjecture confirmed for the model

evidence.title: An inviscid dyadic model of turbulence: the global attractor
evidence.finding: SELF-DISSIPATION: after the blow-up time all solutions stay in H^s, s < 5/6, for almost all time and the energy dissipates; the unique equilibrium is an exponential global attractor

structural_knobs_that_flip_blowup.title: Finite-time blowup for the Fourier-restricted Euler and hypodissipative Navier-Stokes model equations
structural_knobs_that_flip_blowup.quote_verbatim: The Fourier-restricted Euler and hypodissipative Navier--Stokes equations respect both the energy equality and the identity for enstrophy growth from the full Euler and hypodissipative Navier--Stokes equations respectively, which is a substantial advance over the previous literature on Euler and Navier--Stokes model equations.
structural_knobs_that_flip_blowup.structural_note: the (u.grad)u nonlinearity is UNCHANGED; only the Helmholtz projection is replaced by projection onto a more restrictive constraint space with a dyadic shell structure built iteratively using permutations

structural_knobs_that_flip_blowup.knob: the cascade-regularization vs artificial-interaction dichotomy, stated outright
structural_knobs_that_flip_blowup.title: Finite-time blow-up in an elementary model of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations
structural_knobs_that_flip_blowup.quote_verbatim: Previously studied models either exhibit a turbulent cascade that regularizes the three-dimensional viscous dynamics, or rely on highly artificial interactions not transparently realized in the true Euler nonlinearity.
structural_knobs_that_flip_blowup.forward_agenda_quote_verbatim: We conclude with a discussion of the prospects for embedding the behavior of the dyadic model into the full Euler and Navier-Stokes equations.

independent_corroboration.title: How close are shell models to the 3D Navier-Stokes equations?
independent_corroboration.note: the title is this leg's gate question verbatim
independent_corroboration.method: Reynolds-number dependence of velocity and derivative estimates
independent_corroboration.quote_verbatim: It turns out that only the estimate of the mean energy dissipation rate is the same in both systems. The estimates of the velocity and its higher-order derivatives display a weaker Reynolds number dependence for shell models than for the 3D NSEs. Indeed, the velocity-derivative estimates for shell models are found to be equivalent to those corresponding to a velocity gradient averaged version of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations (VGA-NSEs), while the velocity estimates are even milder.
independent_corroboration.placement_verdict: shell models are STRICTLY WEAKER than 3D NS; their exact equivalent is named as a velocity-gradient-averaged NS

independent_corroboration.title: Dynamics of vorticity moments in shell models of turbulence: A comparison with the Navier-Stokes equations
independent_corroboration.method: differential inequalities for vorticity moments / L^{2m} norms
independent_corroboration.quote_verbatim: The contribution of the nonlinear term turns out to be much weaker than its equivalent for the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations. Consequently, pointwise-in-time estimates are shown to exist for the vorticity moments for shell models of any order. ... it is shown that the estimates for shell models formally correspond to those for the Navier-Stokes equations 'on a point'.
independent_corroboration.placement_verdict: shell nonlinearity WEAKER than 3D NS's; correspondence is to NS 'on a point'

independent_corroboration.title: Dyadic models for fluid equations: a survey
independent_corroboration.note: a DEDICATED SURVEY of the hierarchy, by two of the three author names the leg spec asked to be searched for

corroboration_note: Three independent methods — sharp nonlinear estimates (Cheskidov 2006), Reynolds scaling of derivative estimates (Vincenzi-Gibbon 2020), vorticity moments (Gibbon-Vincenzi 2024) — each place 3D NS relative to the shell hierarchy, and none contradicts another. The placement question is answered three times over and cross-checked.

wall_1_reading.wall_1_statement: A search can only argue FOR blow-up, never for regularity (plan_of_record.py:75, CLAY_ROADMAP.md:32, README.md:86).
wall_1_reading.finding_direction: NEGATIVE for the programme, reported against interest
points: At 3D NS's own calibration point alpha = 2/5 the dyadic hierarchy is UNDECIDED — it supplies no blow-up evidence for 3D NS.

Every step toward retaining more genuine NS structure moves the blow-up threshold AWAY from NS: sabra (NS-like sign structure) is globally regular; Miller's enstrophy-respecting model blows up only at alpha < 0.26416 against NS's alpha = 1; forward cascade is itself regularizing; the inviscid dyadic model self-dissipates past its own blow-up time.
Vincenzi-Gibbon and Gibbon-Vincenzi both measure the shell nonlinearity as WEAKER than 3D NS's, with the shell correspondence being NS 'on a point'.

Conclusion: the hierarchy's blow-up results have consistently come from the structure the models DISCARD, not the structure they KEEP — which is why the hierarchy has never transferred to the real equations, and why Palasek's newest paper must spend its conclusion on the embedding question.
